doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

title: Drugs and politics among players; Maynard Ferguson's band
summary: Hal discusses cocaine and drugs among musicians, and his two weeks replacing Chet Ferretti in Maynard Ferguson's band.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Oh I know. It’s that easy. I mean you have to really be on the ball and if you aren’t then you’re gone a lot of times unless you’re really close to the contractor. And you know there are times, and you can cut this out of the thing if you want, but there were times back in the early days when guys would have these little vials of cocaine and during breaks take the contractor out and then come back and they’d always make sure that guy was in their next job. And you know it’s kind of political. I hate to say it but it isn’t just because you’re a good player. Sometimes it’s like what you have to offer too. That was then. Just like on Woody Herman’s band and Maynard’s band there were some junkies and you didn’t have to — I mean the new kids coming up, college graduates, they — as far as I know — they’re pretty clean. You know they don’t do anything like that. They may have some drinks afterwards but I don’t hear of anybody shooting up anymore. And now marijuana is like something where in a lot of states it’s legal now. But at that time, you know that was, to play jazz you had to either shoot up or turn on. And that was just the way it was. Of course I never did that. I was offered, even when I was on Maynard’s band. Maynard was taking — he was experimenting with LSD, under a doctor’s care. And I was in the band for only two weeks because I took Chet Ferretti’s place. He’s from Buffalo I think, great trumpet player. And he went off with the trombone player that was on the band at the same time — Sonny? I’m not sure now. But they — he had a tour in Europe and he took Chet Ferretti and the rhythm section. So I replaced him on Maynard’s band. But early on, in the ‘50s and ‘60s and earlier there was — drugs were a bigger deal then.
